reading: וואֶהרענד דיא כהנים צום דוכן געהען, בעטעט דיא געמיינדע ותערב.
meaning: Literal German (Währenddie Kohanim zum Dukhan gehen, betet die Gemeinde 'Ve-te'erav'): 'While the Kohanim go up to the dukhan (the platform for the priestly blessing), the congregation prays Ve-te'erav.'

characters.evidence: After the double vav there is a separate glyph with a hooked foot at the lower left. It matches the Rashi alef that ends both instances of דיא on this line, and it matches the same opening on PDF256 (german-256-000.jpg). A segol sits clearly under it. The shape is too wide and has the wrong foot to be part of the double vav, so this is not וועהרענד: there is no ע here, and the first ע in the word comes only after ה.

characters.reading: ו ו _ ה ר ע נ ד

characters.evidence: The glyph has a stroke that rises above x-height and a curved body, which is why it can look like a lamed. The Rashi tsadi in this typeface also has a raised top-right stroke, though. Nothing else on this line has a lamed or a tsadi in the same small type to compare it against. At the available scan resolution I cannot cleanly tell a short tsadi flag from a full lamed ascender. ו and ם are clear.
characters.confidence: medium-low on glyph evidence alone; I am not using German grammar as evidence

characters.word: כהנים דוכן געהען בעטעט געמיינדע ותערב

unresolved_disputes: Initial letter of צום/לום: is it a Rashi tsadi or a lamed? The scan alone does not settle it.
recommended_uncertainty_markup: Do not mark the alef in וואֶהרענד as uncertain: it is visibly printed and has a segol. Encode it plainly as וואֶהרענד.

Mark the first letter of צום with cert=low, e.g. <c cert="low">צ</c>ום, or use <choice><unclear cert="low">צ</unclear>…</choice> if you want to record ל as an alternative. It should stay low until someone checks a higher-resolution scan or a confirmed tsadi or lamed in this same small Rashi type on a nearby page.
verdict: Read וואֶהרענד, not וועהרענד: the alef with segol is visible, matches the alef in דיא, and matches the PDF256 glyph. It should be encoded as certain. Read the next word as צום with the initial tsadi at cert=low; the scan does not visually rule out lamed. A tei:c cert=low on the tsadi is a faithful documentary resolution. Putting cert=low on the alef is not necessary and would understate what the page shows. The 'approved' flag applies only to the tsadi markup. This is not full-batch acceptance.
